artifacts.summary: Research on wiring milestone-review-handoff.sh to review-stack-prepare.sh's landed cut/show subcommands: exact interface, exit-code/refusal mechanics, fixture reuse pattern for a successful cut, and two out-of-file_scope findings (narrower file_scope than the parent plan's Phase 5 file list; a test-orchestrate-conclusion-roadmap.sh assertion that will break).

memory_candidates.content: review-stack-prepare.sh's refusal mechanism (rsp_refuse -> exit "$code" called from a plain statement, never inside "$(...)") lets a caller safely capture combined stdout+stderr and branch on $? -- every resolver that can refuse must be invoked unwrapped for this to hold, since exit inside a command-substitution subshell would only kill the subshell.

A push grant's HEAD_SHA is fixed at mint time (push-grant-lib.sh pg_grant_write/pg_grant_mint) and must equal current HEAD to be consumed, so any commit between typing /please and using the grant invalidates it silently -- worth stating explicitly in any UI that prints a /please command to the user.

An expansion record's declared file_scope can be narrower than the section of the parent plan it expands (e.g. a phase's own 'Files to modify' list naming doc files an expansion task's file_scope omits). Check the task's actual file_scope against the parent plan's phase file list before assuming the phase's full file list is in scope; treat any delta as a separate follow-up record rather than silently widening edits.
